entries.title: Headings with #
entries.summary: One `#` makes a title, two make a section heading, three a subsection, four a deeper heading.
entries.syntax:
# Title
## Section heading
### Subsection heading
#### Deeper heading
entries.gotcha: Leave a space after the `#`. Written as `#Title` (no space) it stays plain text in most renderers.

entries.title: Paragraphs and line breaks
entries.summary: End a line with two spaces and press Enter to start the next line on its own; a blank line starts a new paragraph.
entries.syntax:
first line␣␣
second line

new paragraph
entries.example:
The Top 3 movies on IMDB are listed below.  
They are ranked by user rating.

This sentence starts a new paragraph.
entries.output_html:
The Top 3 movies on IMDB are listed below.
They are ranked by user rating.

This sentence starts a new paragraph.
entries.gotcha: Without the two trailing spaces or a blank line, Markdown glues consecutive lines into one paragraph.

entries.title: Bulleted and numbered lists
entries.summary: Start each line with `-`, `*` or `+` for a bullet, or with `1.` for a numbered list.
entries.example:
The Top 3 movies on IMDB are:

- The Shawshank Redemption
- The Godfather
- The Dark Knight

In order:

1. The Shawshank Redemption
1. The Godfather
1. The Dark Knight
entries.output_html:
The Top 3 movies on IMDB are:

  • The Shawshank Redemption
  • The Godfather
  • The Dark Knight

In order:

  1. The Shawshank Redemption
  2. The Godfather
  3. The Dark Knight
entries.gotcha: The numbers you type do not matter: `1.` on every line still renders as 1, 2, 3. Put a blank line before the first item so the list does not merge into the paragraph above it.

entries.title: Bold with **
entries.summary: Wrap text in two asterisks on each side to make it bold.
entries.gotcha: No spaces just inside the asterisks: `** this **` will not turn bold.

entries.title: Italic with *
entries.summary: Wrap text in one asterisk on each side to make it italic.
entries.gotcha: One asterisk is italic, two are bold, three are both: `***loud***`.

entries.title: Inline code with backticks
entries.summary: Wrap a word in single backticks to show it in code style inside a sentence.
entries.example: The backtick key sits left of the number 1 on your keyboard. Use `print()` to show a value.
entries.output_html: The backtick key sits left of the number 1 on your keyboard. Use print() to show a value.
entries.gotcha: The backtick ` is not the single quote '. On most keyboards it is on the key left of 1, also called backquote or grave accent.

entries.title: Fenced code block
entries.summary: Three backticks on their own line open a code block; three more close it. Name the language after the opening fence for coloring.
entries.example:
Demo code that is shown, not run:

```python
print("Hello, world!")
```
entries.output_html:
Demo code that is shown, not run:

print("Hello, world!")
entries.gotcha: Code inside a text cell is never executed. To run it, put it in a code cell instead.

entries.title: Hyperlinks
entries.summary: Put the clickable text in square brackets and the URL in parentheses right after it.
entries.gotcha: Square brackets first, then parentheses. The other order shows literal brackets.

entries.title: Images
entries.summary: An image is a link with an exclamation mark in front. The HTML `` tag does the same and lets you set a width.
entries.gotcha: The address must point at the image file itself (ending in `.png`, `.jpg`), not at a web page that shows the image.

entries.title: Blockquotes with >
entries.summary: Start a line with `>` to set it off as a quotation or a callout box.
entries.example: > **Kind reminder:** give every variable a meaningful name.
entries.output_html: Kind reminder: give every variable a meaningful name.
entries.gotcha: Each line of a multi-line quote needs its own `>`.

entries.title: Tables
entries.summary: Pipes separate the columns; the second line of dashes separates the header from the rows.
entries.syntax:
| Column A | Column B |
|---|---|
| value | value |
entries.output_html:
Type Example Mutable?
str 'success' no
list ['a', 5] yes
entries.gotcha: The line of dashes is required. Without it you get one long paragraph full of pipes. A colon in that line (`:--:`) centers the column.
entries.source: hudm5001_mini/01_Python_Quick_Start.ipynb cell 4 and the Quick Reference tables

entries.title: Horizontal rule with ---
entries.summary: Three dashes on a line of their own draw a horizontal line to separate sections.
entries.example:
End of part 1.

---

Start of part 2.
entries.gotcha: Leave a blank line above the dashes. Directly under a line of text, `---` turns that text into a heading instead.

entries.title: Collapsible block with <details>
entries.summary: Markdown accepts plain HTML. The `<details>` tag hides content behind a clickable `<summary>` line, which is how the notebooks hide solutions.
entries.example:
<details>
<summary>▶ Show solution</summary>

The mean GPA is 3.5.

</details>
entries.output_html:
<details>
<summary>▶ Show solution</summary>

The mean GPA is 3.5.

</details>
entries.gotcha: Leave a blank line after `<summary>` and before `</details>` so that Markdown inside the block (code fences, bold) is still rendered.
